bug_semantics: MessagePackReader.ReadDateTime deserializes a timestamp extension by calling MessagePackPrimitives.TryReadDateTime, which sets tokenSize = checked((int)header.Length) from the attacker-controlled MessagePack extension body length and returns DecodeResult.InsufficientBuffer when the current span is shorter than that size, before checking that only the legal timestamp encodings (4, 8, or 12 bytes) are present. The reader's InsufficientBuffer slow path then does stackalloc byte[tokenSize]. A tiny Ext32 payload can therefore declare a huge timestamp body, force a single-frame stack allocation large enough to throw an uncatchable StackOverflowException, and terminate the host. MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData and MaximumObjectGraphDepth do not apply because the crash is not object-graph recursion. The CWE-789 fix is to reject non-{4,8,12} lengths before any insufficient-buffer handling so the slow path never stack-allocates from an untrusted body length.
flaw_origin: The DateTime stack-overflow mechanism did not exist in the pre-primitives reader. Parent 8d291e4203a24946034dfe33b4c4faca4d61547e still implemented ReadDateTime as ReadDateTime(ReadExtensionFormatHeader()), and ReadExtensionFormatHeader only checked Remaining >= header.Length then switched on lengths 4/8/12; invalid lengths threw MessagePackSerializationException and the body length was never used as a stackalloc size. Commit 35682022fa24fb341bbd3f08d2bba0e1d2c913ff (Add MessagePackPrimitives class) first wrote TryRead(ReadOnlySpan, ExtensionHeader, out DateTime, out tokenSize) with tokenSize = header.Length before the 4/8/12 switch, and rewrote MessagePackReader.ReadDateTime to stackalloc byte[tokenSize] on InsufficientBuffer. That is a new decoder contract, not a move of the old path. GitHub squash 44f79c1f3e23ff16ecadc22e8c135c449a1890ae later landed the same mechanism on develop via PR #1986.

reasoning: This is a real CWE-789 process-killing DoS, not a withdrawn advisory: CVE-2026-48502 is PUBLISHED and GHSA-382j-8mxh-c7x2 is not withdrawn. The sink is specific to the v3 MessagePackPrimitives DateTime decoder. Before PR #1986, ReadDateTime validated extension type and then switched on legal timestamp sizes 4/8/12 after a Remaining check; an oversized declared length failed with a catchable serialization exception and never became a stackalloc size. 35682022fa24fb341bbd3f08d2bba0e1d2c913ff first wrote the new TryRead DateTime contract that publishes tokenSize from the untrusted body length and returns InsufficientBuffer before the 4/8/12 switch, plus the ReadDateTime slow path that stackallocs that tokenSize. Immediate parent 8d291e4203a24946034dfe33b4c4faca4d61547e lacks MessagePackPrimitives.Readers.cs and the stackalloc path, so this is a first-write rather than a move. Mainline 44f79c1f3e23ff16ecadc22e8c135c449a1890ae is a GitHub squash of PR #1986 and is therefore not the BIC; public member 35682022 was reconstructed from the pre-force-push PR head 8a63bce (Readers.cs blob identical on rebased 97a95c32). That BIC is a GPG-signed Andrew Arnott commit with no AI trailers, so the verdict is NOT_AI. The independent fix 26d4e743ca2a88a5626e62cced3762820e392325 validates 4/8/12 before insufficient-buffer handling, is the commit cited for GHSA-382j-8mxh-c7x2 in the v3.1.7 notes, and first appears in v3.1.7, matching the GHSA patched boundary.
